# fied

> Share your tmux session in the browser with end-to-end encryption. One command: `npx fied`.

fied attaches to a running tmux session, generates a 256-bit AES encryption key, and connects to a relay server. Viewers open a link in their browser to see and interact with the terminal in real time. The encryption key is placed in the URL fragment (#), which is never sent to the server — the relay forwards opaque encrypted bytes and cannot read the terminal content.

- Zero config: just run `npx fied` with a running tmux session
- End-to-end encrypted: AES-256-GCM with random IVs per message
- Interactive: viewers can type, not just watch
- View-only links: share read-only access separately
- Background mode: share persists after closing the terminal
- Up to 5 concurrent viewers per session
- Auto-reconnect on network interruptions
- Self-hostable: the relay is a Cloudflare Worker

## Usage

- [GitHub README](https://github.com/gstohl/fied#readme): Installation, usage examples, and self-hosting instructions
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/fied): Package details and version history

## Architecture

fied is a monorepo with four packages:

- `packages/crypto`: AES-256-GCM encryption, key generation, wire protocol framing
- `packages/cli`: CLI tool — attaches to tmux via node-pty, encrypts I/O, connects to relay
- `packages/relay`: Cloudflare Worker + Durable Objects — routes encrypted WebSocket messages
- `packages/web`: Browser viewer — xterm.js terminal, decrypts with key from URL fragment

## Security

- AES-256-GCM with random IV per message
- Key generated on the host machine, placed in URL fragment
- The URL fragment (#) is never sent to the server (RFC 3986 §3.5)
- The relay forwards opaque binary blobs — it cannot read terminal content
- All traffic over WSS (TLS)
- Rate-limited session creation
- Replay protection via per-message nonces
